subject: Clarify default handling: ephemeral vs persistent logs (prompts / outputs)
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@clearexamples.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Default log retention - prompts vs outputs (quick clarifying Q)

Hi Markus / Lauren,

Thanks for walking us through Redwood last week. Before we move forward with a POC, our InfoSec/Privacy team asked a couple of specific clarifications about default telemetry and retention you mentioned on the call. Could you confirm the following for the hosted Redwood API (no dedicated/private contract yet):

- By default, are request inputs (prompts) stored the same way as model outputs? Is there a separation in classification/retention?
- What is the default retention window for request/response telemetry (prompts + completions) and for derived artifacts (embeddings, logs, traces)?
- If a customer requests deletion for a particular record (ex: data subject request or legal hold release), what is the exact deletion flow and SLAs? Do we need a support ticket, or is there a self-serve API?
- Are any runtime caches (KV cache, prefix cache) persisted to disk or replicated to long-term storage by default?

We need these details for our SOC2 scoping and a short compliance checklist. If you have a one-pager or matrix that maps "what counts as stored" to retention and residency, please attach.

Appreciate a clear, short answer we can pass on to our auditors.

Best,
Emma
Emma Li
Privacy Counsel, ClearExamples

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@clearexamples.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Default log retention - prompts vs outputs (quick clarifying Q)

Emma — thanks for the precise questions, great to see the checklist framing. Short answers up front, then a concise walkthrough and next steps. Attaching a retention matrix PDF with the same details.

Short answers:
- Prompts (requests) and outputs (model completions) are both collected as "telemetry" by default on Redwood Hosted and retained for 30 days. They are treated as separate artifact types in our catalog: "request_payload" and "response_payload."
- Derived artifacts: embeddings and analytic traces are retained separately. Default windows: embeddings 90 days, non-sensitive diagnostic traces 30 days.
- Deletion flow: for Hosted customers we require a verified support request to trigger deletion from operational stores; standard SLA is 5 business days for purge from primary telemetry stores, plus up to 30 days for some replicated analytics indices to be garbage-collected. Private deployments / Dedicated customers can configure shorter retention or run a Data Erasure API themselves.
- Runtime caches: short-lived in-memory/KV caches are ephemeral and never persisted to long-term object storage by default. They are excluded from backups and not considered part of "stored logs."

Concise walkthrough (details you can copy to your SOC2 doc):
1) Classification
- "Prompts/Inputs": request_payload; captured at ingestion for routing, billing, and quality monitoring.
- "Outputs/Completions": response_payload; captured as model output artifact.
- "Derived": embeddings, eval artifacts, traces, and aggregated metrics. Each has its own retention bucket.

2) Default retention windows (Hosted)
- request_payload: 30 days
- response_payload: 30 days
- embeddings: 90 days
- model traces / debug logs: 30 days (redacted for PII where applicable)

3) Deletion + proof
- Customer opens a verified support case with record identifiers (if known) or a scope description.
- Engineering runbook initiates purges from primary stores (SLA: 5 business days).
- For audit evidence we provide a deletion confirmation and a short export of retention/log purge job IDs (no payload contents).
- For Private/Dedicated customers we expose a Data Erasure API and admin-run purge.

4) Opt-out and configuration
- Customers can opt out of telemetry collection in Hosted by setting the header "x-redwood-store:none" on requests; note this disables quality monitoring and may affect model troubleshooting.
- Dedicated/Private customers can set custom retention windows and data residency (EU/US) via their contract and the Redwood Console.

Caveats & notes:
- If customers ingest data into a model that triggers downstream storage (for example, user-created artifacts or file uploads), those artifacts are subject to their configured storage policies and may be outside the default telemetry buckets.
- Backups and analytics pipelines may cause a longer tail for deletion in read-only analytic indices; we include that in the SLA above.

Next steps: I can schedule a short call with our compliance engineer to walk your auditors through the playbook and provide the retention matrix we attached. Lauren — can you propose times? Priyom FYI on the Data Erasure API details if Emma wants deeper technical docs.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-default-retention-matrix.pdf (mapping artifact type -> default retention/residency)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@clearexamples.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Default log retention - prompts vs outputs (quick clarifying Q)

Thanks Emma — quick addendum from ops side: two small clarifications so your auditors have precise language they can quote.

- "x-redwood-store:none" is only available for non-billing telemetry; billing and quota metering still produce minimal usage records (timestamped counters) which are kept for 365 days for invoicing/dispute reasons.
- For EU residency requests on Hosted, we can route and store telemetry in our EU region if the customer signs the residency addendum. Default Hosted accounts without the addendum are US-resident.

If that 365-day billing retention is a blocker, we can document a special billing-only export and retention agreement for enterprise customers (requires contract amendment).

Proposed next step: 30-minute call with our compliance engineer + product ops. Are you available Wed or Thurs?

—Lauren
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Li <emma.li@clearexamples.com>

Subject: Re: Default log retention - prompts vs outputs (quick clarifying Q)

Markus / Lauren — this is exactly what we needed, thank you. Two follow-ups before I hand to our auditors:

1) Can you confirm the 30-day default applies only to the Hosted product and that Dedicated/Private customers can reduce retention to as low as 0 days for telemetry (subject to billing constraints you noted)?
2) Please confirm you can provide confirmation artifacts after a purge (job IDs / timestamped confirmation). That will satisfy our evidence requirement.

If you can confirm those two items and share a call invite for Wed AM PST, we'll be ready to move to a POC. I've attached our compliance checklist for your reference.

Best,
Emma
Privacy Counsel, ClearExamples
